extracted.intended_audience: Department of Defense contracting officers, installation commanders, and DoD officials conducting OMB A-76 competitive sourcing studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for conducting OMB A-76 competitive sourcing/cost-comparison studies within DoD, including PWS development, cost measurement, procurement method selection, timetables, and protest handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation compliance and issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: The solicitation is done in accordance with the FAR, Service regulations and any other applicable statutory requirements. Depending on the nature of the services being competitively sourced, either an Invitation For Bid (IFB) or a Request For Proposal (RFP) can be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue solicitations through appropriate channels; choose IFB or RFP by nature of services; treat proposals with standard security protections as in other competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison between in-house estimate (MEO) and private/ISSA proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The fifth step in this process is comparison between the in-house bid and the proposed contract or ISSA price. In the case of sealed bids, the contracting officer opens all bids, to include the in-house estimate and enters the prices on the cost comparison form. In the case of a negotiated or best value procurement, the most advantageous private sector or ISSA proposal is compared against the in-house estimate on the Cost Comparison Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter prices on cost-comparison form; make tentative decisions but subject them to further evaluation for responsiveness and responsibility; for negotiated procurements apply best-value trade-offs when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation for responsiveness and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A tentative decision based on cost-comparison data is announced, subject to evaluation for responsiveness and responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each offeror (including MEO) meets responsiveness requirements and responsibility standards before final award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest handling and expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: The final step in the cost comparison process is the resolution of any protests by unsuccessful offerors, whether they be private sector, ISSA or an in-house organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate protests as a routine possibility; there are no steps contracting officers can take to fully mitigate this final step — manage and resolve protests in accordance with applicable procedures and law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Savings threshold for contractor award
rubrics_metrics.description: For a commercial activity to be awarded to a contractor, the bid from that contractor must meet a savings threshold of 10 percent of personnel costs or $10 million over the performance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If threshold not met the activity remains in-house; in best-value procurements trade-offs may allow award despite thresholds if MEO performance adjustments are made and re-compared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) completeness and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: A Performance Work Statement is a statement of the technical functional and performance characteristics of the work to be performed, identifies essential functions to be performed, determines performance factors, including the location of the work, the units of work, the quantity of work units, and the quality and timeliness of the work units. It serves as the scope of the work and the basis for all costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PWS must accurately reflect all activities involved; poor PWSs have led to legal exposure, poor performance, hidden/omitted costs, and contract price adjustments. Prepare PWSs with properly trained integrated teams and legal/document-writing review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate capture and standardization of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: With no standard currently used to measure Government operating costs, DoD has looked to implement Activity Based Costing as a process for capturing the costs of performing commercial activities. The supplement to OMB A-76 provides guidance in calculating these costs but is often silent on specific costs installations face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent, defensible costing methods (consider Activity Based Costing) to capture total costs; watch for hidden costs from poorly-constructed PWSs; document methods because GAO has criticized unreliable savings estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of studies (study completion timeframes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently, single activity studies must be completed within 18 months, while multi-service studies have 36 months to be completed. Past average time to complete an A-76 study was 4 years and 3 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan resources to meet the ambitious mandated timeframes; be aware that shortening timeframes may impact study quality and completion rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and competency of personnel to conduct studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Continued downsizing has meant fewer personnel familiar with the A-76 process capable of conducting the studies; availability of experienced civil service employees to participate in PWS development has been problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure sufficient trained staff or provide training; consider outsourcing parts of studies only if inherently governmental functions and in-house cost-estimating remain government-led; use Integrated Process Teams (IPTs) with experienced members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear definition and listing of commercial activities vs inherently governmental functions
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB A-76 lists numerous functions within broad categories that qualify as commercial services. However, there is no consensus among Services or installation commanders as to what constitutes a commercial activity or an inherently Governmental function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile and maintain authoritative lists (FAIR Act requires yearly lists), consolidate definitions across commands where possible, and resolve service-level differences before initiating studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting officer oversight during acquisition strategy and PWS development
rubrics_metrics.description: Oversight by the Contracting Officer during the development of the acquisition strategy is the primary place one would expect to catch discrepancies in the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage contracting officer early and throughout PWS and acquisition strategy development to detect drafting errors, omissions, or legal vulnerabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrated Product/Process Teams, involvement of key management personnel, early contracting officer involvement, local union participation, and keeping Government employees informed were repeatedly cited as important lessons learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage stakeholders early (IPTs), ensure senior leadership support/steering groups enforce quality and timelines, involve unions where required, and communicate to affected employees to reduce resistance and misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards for conflicts of interest and potential misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is the potential for misrepresentation on the part of A-76 team members in an effort to keep their jobs; while unlikely, it must be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement safeguards and oversight to detect and deter misrepresentation or sabotage by team members (ethical rules, conflict-of-interest rules, CO oversight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with statutory legal restrictions on outsourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific legal restrictions include the prohibition against outsourcing fire fighting and policing services aboard installations. Additionally, congressional mandates can require a given percentage of depot maintenance be performed by Government employees. Past Defense Authorization Acts and appropriations language have sometimes restricted contracting of activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify statutory and appropriations restrictions before including activities in competitive sourcing; consult legal advisors to confirm eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate selection of procurement method and evaluation approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on the nature of the services, either IFB, RFP, sealed bid, negotiated/best value, or direct conversion may be used; 8(a) sole source techniques and direct conversions have been applied in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the procurement vehicle consistent with law/regulation and the nature of the acquisition; when using best value, perform trade-off analyses between contractor proposals and the MEO; document rationale for method selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance and retention of in-house oversight capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk identified: not having Government personnel qualified to 'inspect' contractor functions as part of Quality Assurance Evaluation; loss of in-house expertise over time makes it difficult to survey contractor performance and re-write contracts after the initial contract is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain or train in-house QA personnel, preserve institutional knowledge needed to monitor contractors and prepare future acquisitions or contract modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete capture of workload data and clear units of work
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to adequately capture the workload data that must be accomplished by an organization is a concern; PWS must define units of work, quantity, quality and timeliness. Poor capture leads to hidden costs and contract adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect robust workload measurements, define units of work clearly in PWS, and ensure costing methods align to measured workloads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk identification and mitigation (manpower, worker reaction, contractor quality, SOW boundaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant risks include worker reaction to competitive sourcing, minimal manpower levels, inability to find quality contractors, poorly scoped SOW/PWS that add work inadvertently, and decreased performance when costs are cut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify, document, and mitigate risks: workforce engagement strategies, staffing plans, contractor market research/qualification, careful scoping to avoid adding work to MEO if not intended, and QA monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic expectation and measurement of projected savings
rubrics_metrics.description: While past A-76 competitions have yielded cost savings (examples 27%-36%), GAO and RAND have questioned projected savings and pointed out factors that can undermine savings (mandated wage increases, poorly written PWSs, contract modifications/price adjustments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be conservative in savings projections, use reliable data and standardized costing methods, and plan for post-award contract management that may reveal and correct PWS deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Integrated Product/Process Teams (IPTs) and strong steering groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents emphasized the importance of Integrated Product Teams and strong steering groups to instill quality, enforce timelines, and involve key functional experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form IPTs with appropriate functional representation, ensure steering groups provide leadership oversight and enforce schedule/quality controls.
